purpose: Static design previews; scale ratios are prompt targets, not measured game coordinates.

variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Precise screenshot edit for a series comparing world minimap scales. The attached image is the EDIT TARGET: MicroCol's game screen with a clean atlas minimap at top right. Return the COMPLETE screenshot, exactly matching input composition and aspect ratio. Preserve everything outside the minimap interior: main game map, toolbar, sidebar player info, hints, status bar, typography, unit positions, dimensions and palette. Do not restyle the screen.
Keep the minimap frame exactly the same position and size as reference, approx x=1340..1556, y=128..318 in a 1578x997 output (216x190). Only replace the geography and viewport INSIDE this frame. The full rectangular playable-world extent is always fitted inside that fixed frame, north up. This is a schematic DESIGN illustration of a larger world, not a map of Earth.
STYLE FIXED FOR ALL VARIANTS: flat muted teal water, sage green grassland, darker olive forest areas, small ochre highlands, occasional gray rocky patches, strongly inked 2-3px slightly hand-drawn known coastlines; NO tree/ship/unit icons, tile grid, names, text labels or decorative textures. Solid opaque taupe gray-beige fog masks 55-65% of the minimap, hiding all underlying terrain and coasts. Unknown areas must show no clues to hidden geography. Two sparse small question marks inside unknown areas only.
Unlike the original overly close-up minimap, this variant is MUCH MORE ZOOMED OUT: the recognizable current coastal bend and the white viewport must be SMALL relative to the minimap. Show an illustrative broader explored coastline and turquoise sea corridor continuing beyond that little current view, while large irregular blocks of unknown cover the map's periphery and some interior. The additional explored surroundings are schematic design context, not new gameplay claims. Keep distant topography coarse but more geographic context visible as scale shrinks. The recognizable local shape inside the viewport is green land WEST, turquoise water EAST with a small lake and southward river/bend like the attached main game map. The tiny current viewport is at 40% of minimap width, 45% of minimap height; wider explored coast can continue north and south of it. Frame is a CLOSED landscape RECTANGLE with unfilled interior, cream-white stroke over thin dark keyline; aspect 1.62:1, square corners, not a square. Exactly one viewport. No handles, ticks, extra rectangles, rulers or scale labels inside the game UI.
Keep the outside game scene entirely unchanged; scale differences apply ONLY within the top-right minimap. Do not zoom the whole screenshot, do not increase minimap size. The output should look like the same screen with one different world minimap reduction.
SCALE VARIANT 1: the entire minimap's width represents 3 main-map-view widths. Therefore the viewport rectangle MUST be 72px wide by 44px tall in the 216x190 minimap, exactly ONE THIRD of minimap width. Compared to the reference, shrink the locally recognizable coastal area and surround it with a wider world context. The viewport should frame the complete local coastal bend, not just its northern tip.
